slot.brief: Count the number of n-digit numbers formed from a given digit multiset satisfying a condition such as divisibility by 5 or digits in increasing order; split into cases.

stem: How many six-digit numbers divisible by $5$ can be obtained by rearranging all the digits of $110025$?
working:
Last digit $0$: $\dfrac{5!}{2!}-\dfrac{4!}{2!}=48$. Last digit $5$: $\dfrac{5!}{2!2!}-\dfrac{4!}{2!}=18$. Total $=48+18=66$.

Independent check: Ending in 0: 5!/2! − 4!/2! = 48. Ending in 5: 5!/(2!2!) − 4!/2! = 18. Total = 66.
solution:
A number divisible by $5$ must end in $0$ or $5$.
Ending in $0$: $\dfrac{5!}{2!}-\dfrac{4!}{2!}=48$; ending in $5$: $\dfrac{5!}{2!2!}-\dfrac{4!}{2!}=18$.
Hence, total numbers $=48+18=66$.
